rationale: Scope clarification for the C1 obligation so the review issue of the superseded artifact can be answered on the claim's own terms: the claim now names the applied-state proposition as C3's and states where its own obligation ends.
new_basis: The applied-state proposition was fixed as its own claim (C3) with its own reviewed check, and the C1 artifact that asserted it was challenged on scope. Amending C1's scope to name that attribution removes the ambiguity the challenge identified without changing the obligation, its conditions or its artifacts.

claims.description: When recovery runs for instance (Replica, Instance) and a slow-quorum PrepareReply reports that instance COMMITTED with a command vector, the recovering replica must adopt that committed vector (Status COMMITTED carrying the committed commands) rather than continuing from its own record and restarting phase 1 with a different command.

scope.description: Recovery decision for a single instance on the captured snapshot: N=3 with Thrifty and IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding only a default NONE record, one peer holding a COMMITTED record with a real command, and no third replica reply required. The obligation ends at adopting the reported committed vector; what each replica then applies is a separate obligation (claim C3).
assumptions: the recovering replica's own record carries no commands
a slow quorum (its own entry plus one reply) is sufficient to resolve
messages are delivered through the real wire format
excluded: producing the committed record through a real proposal, accept round and commit broadcast
configurations with N>3 or a live leader flag

execution of the instance and client-visible replies; applied-state agreement for a committed instance is claim C3-applied-effect-follows-committed-vector's proposition and is not part of this obligation

grounding.derivation: Recovery exists to carry the value that could have been committed across a change of leader. In this snapshot the recovering replica seeds its bookkeeping from its own record, makes a new ballot and reports that new ballot as its own VBallot, while handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of a reply only when element.VBallot >= the running lb.ballot. The responsibility asserted here is that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted, because a committed record is the authoritative value for that instance and is the only input that can keep the recovering replica consistent with replicas that already installed the commit.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the captured snapshot with N=3 and Thrifty, IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding a default NONE record for the instance and one slow-quorum peer holding a COMMITTED record with a command; the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance.
unresolved: whether a full legal history (real proposal, accept round, commit broadcast, execution timeout) reaches the same state
whether the launched configuration permits a replica to hold a default record for an instance that another replica has committed
alternatives: an alternative reading is that the recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal, which the review should test against the cited resolution code

patch.rationale: Replaces the C1 claim with the same id, obligation and sources, adding one clause to the scope description and one excluded item that names C3; no other field changes.

old_judgment: The C1 obligation's scope excluded execution but did not say where the applied-state consequence belongs, which let an artifact assert it under C1.
new_judgment: The C1 obligation ends at adopting the reported committed vector; applied-state agreement for a committed instance is claim C3's proposition, and the scope now says so explicitly.

grounding.derivation: The boundary follows the two obligations already accepted: C1's properties concern the value a recovery adopts, and C3's concern the effect replicas apply from the committed vector, which the executor and state application establish.
grounding.applicability: C1 and C3 as accepted for the N=3 Thrifty configuration.
